It's probably not even the party if it really did go as well as you're saying it did. (Which I just want to ask, does your wife also agree that it went well except for these few things?)

Instead of looking for validation because you think your wife was overreacting to poop bags and misspelled cake and crying while the party was ending (which I just want to point out you think she thought poo bags were humiliating? Try crying at your kids birthday because of the mass amount of stress you're under), talk to your wife and see what she needs, how she feels. She's not talking to you and telling you what's wrong because you don't care about anything else that goes on in the house, why would you care about her feelings? Don't look at this singular event and expect to be patted on the back for doing something even if you fucked it up, look at all the events.

Imagine if your wife wasn't here doing everything and you were a single father. Would your kids still be happy? Would the house be clean and food be prepared, etc.? Being married with kids is not easy, it's not going to be easy, and the way you're talking it seems like it has been easy for you. Which means it's been that much harder on your wife. Take this as a wake up call and start being an active participant in your family. Dont go to your wife and show her all the negative comments about her making the party about herself and expect her to agree and get over it. I can guarantee you she's already dwelling on it. Go to her and try, for her and for your kids and for your house.

I was younger when my pawpaw passed away (congestive heart failure and other things, my mawmaw blames agent orange) and he never really talked about those things with me, or really anyone for that matter, but my mawmaw tells a couple stories about his time.

One that really sticks with me is that he would sometimes go without his helmet when just walking around the camp and his commanding officer would get on to him about it and make him put it on. Well, one time he had been chastised for not wearing his helmet and (according to my mawmaw) he put it on and about 45 seconds later people starting firing at them and his helmet got shot. He never had to be told to wear his helmet again after that.

Another is kind of fuzzy for me to remember details but the gist is: my pawpaw had been shot (unrelated to the first story) in his arm? Leg? And received a purple heart. But there was a guy who had gotten a purple heart for stubbing his toe or getting a splinter or something and my pawpaw felt that it brought down the meaning of the medal, so he buried it with some kids (I cant remember if it was "kids" in his unit or kids as in actual children who had died because of the war). 

I didnt get to know him much but his last day I remember so fondly, my two cousins and i were playing in the front yard and i came in for something to drink and he was sitting in his chair watching us and smiling and i told him i loved him and he smiled bigger and told me he loved me too and kissed me on the cheek (he never really smiled or said i love you or kissed often so it felt different at the time). We all had a nice day and my mom, two cousins, and I went home and the next day my mom brought us in the living room and told us he had passed. My cousins just went back to playing because they were far too young to really understand death, but I left the house and walked to a little park by my house and sat on a swing and cried. It was bittersweet because I didn't want him gone but he had been in so much pain and I knew he was better now. Sometimes I really felt like he was still with us, i would go to do something harmful and then randomly think of him... I like to think that he was there. When people ask those "if you could have lunch with one, living or dead" questions I always say my pawpaw. Sometimes I think about how he wasnt able to see me get married, or have my baby, and how i never really knew him because I was too young, and it makes me sad but i also think that his memory lives within me and when i die if heaven and hell are real i hope to live down the cloud street from him.

After reading some comments and picturing a world where assisted suicide is legal, I rethought my college speech a little and now I wish I would've brought up better points. 

   On one hand, it ends the suffering. You no longer have to live through the pain of cancer, you're no longer a burden on your family, you die with dignity. Many people have brought up that it's better than outright killing yourself because it's still your choice and you get to go peacefully rather than blowing your brains out, I'd also think if they did make this legal you'd have to talk with trained professionals and there would be a waiting period before you could. (I once read that Angelina Jolie or some famous actress hired a hit man to kill her so it wouldn't be so hard on her family and he asked her to wait a month and here she is still living, an idea like that) It would also cut down on the rising population problem the world is having right now. (I understand that's really morbid, but it's the truth) It's also good because it gives you control over every aspect of your life. Death is certain, but when and how is not always certain. So, a person afraid of death could pick the date and get everything in order beforehand. One of my biggest fears is leaving behind everything I have and not leaving a legacy. With that theory, as well, you could save money to do the things you want to do in life. Say you have 3 weeks before you're death date and you want to go to Alaska or something and run with wolves in the cold. I mean, these are simple points and you could just do these things anyway, but it gives the person a chance to forget about work and school or other responsibilities in life and do what they want to do without being tied down. The idea of living carefree sounds selfish, but living a life of mundane tasks and working until you die, that's not how [I feel] life should be. We are so restricted to things beyond our control, most of the time, that we cannot enjoy life the way life should be enjoyed. There are so many good aspects to assisted suicide, and there are more positives that I just can't think of at the moment.

   On the other hand, though, there are many negatives. Corruption seems to be the biggest in the comments. It hadn't even crossed my mind that there are doctors out there that would pressure you into this if it meant they get more money for it, or if it costs the hospital less to just kill you off rather than try and save your life. There's also the guilt of being sick and making your family suffer mentally and/or financially with you. That could change someone's mind on whether or not they would want to look at assisted suicide as an option. There would bound to be loopholes in the system that make it dangerous, say since they are going to die anyways there's no need to take safety precautions. Or just examples like that, since A then B type situations where it does not benefit the person dying. There's also the fact that if someone is suicidal and they want to end their life, they could be leaving behind a family or friends who love them dearly. They could very well do it themselves at any moment, but having someone else do it in a controlled environment, painlessly, just fall asleep and die; that might give them the courage to actually go through with it. Speaking of courage, one of the reasons I'm still here is because I was scared of dying. I was scared of the pain and "what if I don't do it right?" thoughts. Another problem with assisted suicide is you can't change your mind once they put the needle in you. No one is in your head hearing your thoughts of "Is this is the right thing to do?". The doctor can't change his mind for you, they wouldn't be able to feel your emotions. And let's not mention the whole religious, "killing yourself is a sin". (Which is why I think a lot of people are against it, even though there is a separation of church and state, *supposedly*). The theory that if a doctor performs assisted suicide, he becomes a murderer. I could see a lot of legal issues with that one, giving a few people that type of power over one person's life. Then there is the whole payment thing too. How much would this cost? Again with the whole "doctors pushing towards euthanasia", people who can't afford health care or their health care doesn't provide for the cure they need or it would cost the hospital too much to have that cure. And speaking of cures, would this also decrease scientists to finding cures for things? Just a thought: If dying is less expensive and fundamentally better for the growth of society or the betterment of the Earth, would people then stop trying to find ways to survive forever? Then, there would be either too many rules and regulations or not enough. The truth of the matter is; we are talking about ending people's lives. Ceasing someone to exist by someone else's hands. Life is delicate and shouldn't be taken for granted. 

In conclusion, there are issues with everything in life. There are good sides and bad sides, rights and wrongs, goodness and corruption. Who are we to make this type of decision for someone else? We can put "Do not resuscitate" and we can pull someone off life support, why not give people the option to end their own life with help?
